string.u: Create an App with Github Url Repo

resources.string: The icon is resized into these resource folders:
Open the project structure to pick a file.
Let an AI assistant (Claude, ChatGPT or Gemini) read and edit your projects and start builds. It reaches this phone through a relay server that you own.
The address of your own MCP relay. It is saved on this phone only. The project includes a ready-to-deploy relay in the relay folder.
Enter a valid https:// relay address, without ? or #.
Enter your relay URL above. The address to paste into your AI appears here.
Anyone who knows your relay URL can reach this phone, so keep it private. Keep read-only mode on unless you want the AI to change files.
Keep the phone online. If the connection drops while the screen is off, turn off battery optimisation for Studio Mobile.

1. Tap Connect above and wait for “Connected”.
2. Open claude.ai or the Claude desktop app → Customize → Connectors → + → Add custom connector.
3. Name it Studio Mobile and paste this as the Remote MCP server URL:
%1$s
Leave sign-in and advanced settings empty.
4. Add it, enable the connector in a chat and ask: “List my Studio Mobile projects.”

Team or Enterprise: an Owner adds it first under Organization settings → Connectors → Add → Custom.

Claude Code has its own entry below.

1. Tap Connect above and wait for “Connected”.
2. On chatgpt.com open Settings → Apps & Connectors → Advanced settings and turn on Developer mode. Your plan must support it, for example Plus or Pro.
3. Create a connector named Studio Mobile. MCP server URL:
%1$s
Authentication: No authentication. Tick “I trust this application”, then Create.
4. Start a new chat, tap + → More → Developer mode and select Studio Mobile.

Menu names change between releases; look for custom connectors and Developer mode.

Gemini connects through Gemini CLI.
1. Tap Connect above and wait for “Connected”.
2. Run this in a terminal:
gemini mcp add --transport http --scope user studio-mobile %1$s
Or add it to ~/.gemini/settings.json:
{"mcpServers":{"studio-mobile":{"httpUrl":"%1$s"}}}
Use httpUrl, not url: url means SSE.
3. Start gemini and type /mcp to check that studio-mobile is connected.
Only needed when your relay was started with PHONE_TOKEN. Saved on this phone only.

Any client that supports remote MCP servers over HTTP works.

Claude Code:
claude mcp add --transport http studio-mobile %1$s

If your relay was started with AI_TOKEN, add the header:
claude mcp add --transport http studio-mobile %1$s --header "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_AI_TOKEN"

Or put this in .mcp.json in your project:
{"mcpServers":{"studio-mobile":{"type":"http","url":"%1$s","headers":{"Authorization":"Bearer YOUR_AI_TOKEN"}}}}

Gemini CLI takes the same header: add --header "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_AI_TOKEN" to the gemini mcp add command.

Clients that only speak stdio can use a bridge:
npx -y mcp-remote %1$s

The ChatGPT connector form has no header field, so do not set AI_TOKEN on a relay that ChatGPT uses.
On: the AI can only read. Off: it can also edit, add, move and delete files, change Gradle files and start builds.
